entry.title: Kadoa Report Finds Investor-Owned Utilities Charge 23% More For Electricity Than Public Providers
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | kadoa.com | hacker news

In 2025, residential electricity customers paid an average of 17.8 cents per kilowatt-hour at investor-owned utilities, compared to 14.5 cents at public utilities and 14.1 cents at co-ops. Since 2020, investor-owned utility prices increased by 34%, outpacing both public utility price growth of 19% and general inflation of 24%.

The widening price gap primarily developed between 2020 and 2023 during a broad energy price spike, with investor-owned rates rising 25% while nonprofit utility rates rose 11%. Investor-owned utilities build shareholder returns into their rate structures, whereas public utilities and co-ops operate without shareholders and often benefit from tax exemptions and tax-free borrowing.

entry.title: Microsoft AI Diagnostic System Outperforms Doctors in Complex Case Study
entry.content:
TechCrunch AI | techcrunch.com | source

Microsoft’s MAI-DxO diagnostic system, which coordinates multiple AI agents to simulate a clinical panel, correctly diagnosed complex medical cases 83% of the time in a simulation based on New England Journal of Medicine cases. By comparison, generalist physicians working individually with reference materials achieved an accuracy rate of 36% on the same complex cases.

Revealed in a study published in Science, the system achieved its highest accuracy when paired with OpenAI’s GPT-5 and GPT-5.5 models, though performance gains varied when applied to emergency department cases. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman noted that the work is part of a broader push toward medical superintelligence, with upcoming foundational healthcare models planned in partnership with the Mayo Clinic and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.

entry.title: Anthropic Claude Model Designs Protein Binders Against Scorpion Neurotoxins
entry.content:
Techmeme | anthropic.com | hacker news

Anthropic tasked an internal research model within Claude Science to design protein minibinders targeting scorpion neurotoxins in collaboration with Citrini Research. Over a 64-hour autonomous campaign, the model generated over 318,000 designs, of which 211 were lab-tested by Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience, yielding 17 designs that met strict binding criteria across four dangerous scorpion neurotoxins.

Although the binders have not yet been tested for cellular neutralization or in living animals, outside experts consider the results a promising initial step for accelerating neglected tropical disease research. Anthropic has released all 211 designs and their corresponding binding data publicly on Hugging Face to encourage further scientific development.

entry.title: Study Finds Deep-Sea Life in Gulf of Mexico Has Not Recovered 16 Years After Deepwater Horizon Spill
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | e360.yale.edu | source | hacker news

A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences reveals that populations of deep-sea animals such as octopus, squid, krill, shrimp, and lanternfish in the Gulf of Mexico declined by at least 60 percent following the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and have shown no measurable signs of recovery.

Researchers identified lingering oil-related compounds in the tissues and eggs of deep-dwelling species, which can impair reproduction, development, and survival. The findings suggest that the deep-pelagic biome possesses limited resilience to severe human-induced disturbances, alongside concerning reductions in genetic diversity.

entry.title: UNEP Releases Emissions Gap Report 2026 on 1.5°C Overshoot
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | unric.org | source | hacker news

The United Nations Environment Programme has published its 2026 Emissions Gap Report, warning that the Paris Agreement goal of limiting global warming to 1.5°C is no longer achievable within the decade. Titled "The Point of Return," the report states that exceeding the 1.5°C threshold is now imminent and unavoidable, requiring a new strategy to limit peak warming and bring temperatures back down by the end of the century.

To keep warming below 2°C and eventually return to 1.5°C, the report outlines that global greenhouse gas emissions must fall by 18 percent by 2030, 45 percent by 2035, and 69 percent by 2040 relative to 2025 levels. Current national climate commitments fall significantly short of these benchmarks, achieving only modest reductions and highlighting a severe leadership gap in global climate action.

entry.title: Steve Krouse Examines the Purpose of Education in Feld of AGI
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | stevekrouse.com | hacker news

Programmer and soon-to-be father Steve Krouse explores the evolving purpose of education as artificial general intelligence (AGI) reshapes traditional skill sets and career trajectories. Reflecting on how his own economic value as a software developer feels compromised, he questions what knowledge and values remain vital to impart to the next generation.

Drawing on Neil Postman’s 1995 book The End of Education and historical false alarms regarding educational technology—such as Thomas Edison’s 1913 prediction that books would become obsolete—Krouse examines how institutional schooling endures through shifting societal needs. Ultimately, he suggests that as traditional economic incentives wobble, parents and educators must collaboratively forge new narratives and purposes for learning.

entry.title: Single-Motor Drone Design Uses Hinged Propeller for Flight Control
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | youtube.com | hacker news

A single-motor drone design achieves pitch and roll control through a hinged propeller hub that responds to rapid changes in motor acceleration. This approach reduces mechanical complexity compared to quadcopters but requires highly complex firmware and precise motor control to manage directional changes.

The project utilizes a Motius R4 servo controller to manage motor speeds up to 20,000 RPM and an infrared lighthouse system for heading information. While the design aims to make drones smaller and cheaper, the implementation faces significant challenges with vibrations and rotational stability caused by high-speed propeller-blade movement.

entry.title: CERN and Mistral Partner to Develop AI Foundation Models for Physics
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | home.cern | hacker news

CERN and Mistral have signed a statement of intent to establish a long-term strategic partnership to develop foundation models for scientific discovery. The collaboration aims to create the first "Large Physics Model" for collider physics, which will be trained on simulated proton-proton collisions from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) to perform tasks such as particle reconstruction, particle identification, and signal flagging.

The initiative seeks to transition from using multiple specialized algorithms to using single pretrained models capable of operating across the entire reconstruction chain. The project leverages CERN's exabyte-scale datasets and is designed to scale alongside the High-Luminosity LHC upgrade, which is expected to begin operation around 2030.

entry.title: Organ-on-a-Chip and New Methodologies Gain Traction as Alternatives to Animal Testing
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | spectrum.ieee.org | hacker news

New approach methodologies (NAMs), such as organ-on-a-chip systems and organoids, are increasingly replacing animal models in biomedical research and drug development. Recent regulatory changes, including the FDA Modernization Act 2.0 and 2026 FDA rules, permit the use of non-animal methods in preclinical safety studies. Major institutions like the NIH and the European Commission are also transitioning toward prioritizing human-based research over traditional animal experiments.

Widespread adoption of NAMs requires overcoming challenges in standardization, commercial scalability, and the validation of predictive biomarkers. To be effective, these technologies must move from academic proofs-of-concept to mass-produced, reliable products that provide consistent results. The transition also necessitates significant changes in research culture, training, and global regulatory alignment to ensure data comparability.
